title: Participate in business continuity planning and exercises: decision comparison 2
teachingQuestion: How do business owners turn disruption consequences into continuity priorities, workable alternatives, and evidence from an exercise?
focalInsight: Critical function, BIA, priority, manual workaround, external dependency, communications, and remediation.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Continuity Communications
nodes.definition: Internal and external messages that coordinate roles, affected customers, suppliers, leadership, and transition decisions during disruption.
nodes.decision: Predefine audience, authority, channels, and the difference between exercise status and real-event notices.
nodes.failureExample: Conflicting customer messages can compound disruption even when operations are recovering.
nodes.detail: Internal and external messages that coordinate roles, affected customers, suppliers, leadership, and transition decisions during disruption.

nodes.label: Continuity Remediation
nodes.definition: An owned corrective change that removes or reduces a tested continuity gap and is verified after implementation.
nodes.decision: Prioritize by effect on the critical function, route changes through governance, and retest the altered capability.
nodes.failureExample: Closing a vendor-dependency finding without testing the alternate supplier leaves the continuity gap open.
nodes.detail: An owned corrective change that removes or reduces a tested continuity gap and is verified after implementation.

nodes.label: External Dependency
nodes.definition: A supplier, utility, service, regulator, or other outside party whose availability or decision affects continuity of a function.
nodes.decision: Identify dependency owners, agreements, alternate options, contact paths, and failure assumptions in the plan and exercise.
nodes.failureExample: A continuity plan that assumes a cloud, telecom, or verification vendor is always available fails under shared disruption.
nodes.detail: A supplier, utility, service, regulator, or other outside party whose availability or decision affects continuity of a function.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: How do business owners turn disruption consequences into continuity priorities, workable alternatives, and evidence from an exercise?
learningContract.misconception: Business continuity is simply IT disaster recovery, or a system inventory can set recovery priority.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Critical function, BIA, priority, manual workaround, external dependency, communications, and remediation.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not assign a universal RTO, exercise frequency, or claim a particular supplier SLA.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: The payment platform is intact but the call center and verification vendor are unavailable. Which function, workaround, dependency, and evidence must the exercise test?
